name: Anne van den Ban Fund (ABF) — Wageningen University & Research
duration: Up to 24 months (the duration of the MSc programme)
eligibleNationalities: International students from developing / low-income countries who have secured unconditional admission to a WUR MSc programme. Bangladesh, as a developing/low-income South Asian country, is not on any exclusion list and qualifies. Not for students already studying in Wageningen on a one-year scholarship; this is a separate award from WUR's NL Scholarship (which has a closed country list that excludes Bangladesh).
languageRequirements: Standard Wageningen MSc English-language requirement applies (an accepted English test such as IELTS/TOEFL unless exempted); ABF itself adds no separate language test. Check WUR's 'English language proficiency MSc' page for the exact minimum scores.
standardizedTests: Not required (no GRE/GMAT for WUR MSc admission)
minGPA: Good academic results / outstanding students are required, but WUR does not publish a fixed ABF GPA cut-off. (Sibling WUR invitation scholarships — Excellence, ASP — require a GPA of 80% or higher / First Class honours; ABF favours strong students but its own threshold is not published.)
applicationFee: No separate ABF application fee (it is invitation-only). The standard WUR MSc application page lists no application fee.
fundingCovers: Tuition fee (in full or in part — full and partial scholarships both exist)
Possible contribution to living costs (combined with the WU Fellowship Programme; other income sources are taken into account)
bondObligation: Not a contractual bond, but the fund's stated purpose is that graduates return to their home country to contribute there after graduation.
requiredDocuments: There is NO separate ABF application — candidates are selected only from accepted new MSc students; you must first complete a Wageningen University MSc application by the deadline and gain unconditional admission, then the fund selects by invitation
MSc application: bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in its original language + a certified English translation when the original language is other than English or Dutch
MSc application: original complete/up-to-date transcript of academic records (with a sworn translation if not in English or Dutch)
MSc application: proof of English language proficiency (one of the official tests accepted by Wageningen University, unless exempted)
MSc application: Curriculum Vitae / brief personal history (maximum two pages, in English)
MSc application: personal statement (optional, e.g. if the relevance of your transcript/degree is unclear)

timeline.opens: MSc applications for the September 2026 intake (open in the standard WUR admission cycle)
timeline.deadline: 1 February 2026 (MSc application deadline; ABF candidates are selected only from applicants assessed via this deadline)
timeline.resultsBy: 7 May 2026 (selection results communicated to selected candidates only); offers are made in spring, around May. If you have not received an offer by 1 June, you have not been selected.
timeline.notes: Dates are for academic year 2026-2027 / September 2026 intake, as published on WUR's official 'Master's scholarships' page (accessed 2026-06-18). Anchored as of 2026-06: this is the most recent published cycle; the 2027-2028 cycle had not opened. ABF has no direct application — apply for a WUR MSc by 1 February 2026, secure unconditional admission, then await a possible invitation.

benefits: Full or partial scholarship towards an MSc at Wageningen University & Research (the fund explicitly offers both full AND partial scholarships)
Tuition fee covered in full or in part depending on the award
Possible contribution to living costs (award is combined with the WU Fellowship Programme; other income sources are taken into account)
Awarded for the duration of the MSc programme (up to 24 months)
mustKnow: INVITATION-ONLY: you cannot apply directly to the fund. You must first apply for a WUR MSc by 1 February 2026 and gain UNCONDITIONAL admission; the board then selects candidates once a year from accepted new students (offers in spring, around May).
TWO-STEP: step 1 = secure a WUR MSc admission; step 2 = be selected/invited for the scholarship. No separate scholarship form exists.

NOT GUARANTEED FULL FUNDING: awards are explicitly 'full AND partial' — many are partial and may cover tuition only or in part. Other income (other scholarships, earmarked donations, family support, personal income) is weighed in selection, so you may need to top up living costs.
Combined with the WU Fellowship Programme; for the September start only — not offered to students already enrolled in Wageningen on a one-year scholarship.

Open to students from developing / low-income countries (Bangladesh qualifies); this is distinct from WUR's NL Scholarship, whose closed country list does NOT include Bangladesh — do not confuse the two.
The fund's stated intent is that graduates return to their home country after graduation; there is no contractual bond.
If you have not received an offer by 1 June, you have not been selected.
Sibling WUR invitation scholarships (Excellence, ASP) require GPA ≥ 80% / First Class honours; strong academics materially help an ABF invitation, though ABF's own GPA threshold is not published.
renewalConditions: Awarded for the MSc programme duration; continuation depends on satisfactory study progress (per the WU Fellowship Programme framework). No public per-credit renewal threshold is published by WUR.
postStudyWork: The Netherlands offers a post-study 'orientation year' (zoekjaar) residence permit for graduates of Dutch higher education; however the fund's purpose is that graduates return to their home country.
